headline: LePage Widens Lead in 2nd District as Dunlap Struggles with Turnout
body:
Former Governor Paul LePage has opened a 7-point lead over Democratic opponent Matt Dunlap in Maine's 2nd Congressional District race, according to a new poll that shows the Republican gaining ground among rural voters and men less than three months before the November election.

The University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll, released Tuesday, shows LePage leading Dunlap 48 percent to 41 percent, with 11 percent of voters undecided. The survey of 712 likely voters in the district has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.7 percentage points.

LePage is performing strongly among rural voters and male voters, while Dunlap's support is concentrated in the Bangor area and college towns, the poll found. The results represent a shift from earlier polling in the race, which had shown a tighter contest.

Following the poll's release, the nonpartisan Cook Political Report moved the race from "Likely Republican" to "Lean Republican," reflecting growing confidence in LePage's position.

Dunlap's campaign is scrambling to boost turnout in Aroostook and Washington counties, where the Democrat underperformed in the June primary. The two northernmost counties are traditionally Democratic strongholds, but Dunlap's campaign has acknowledged the need to energize voters there ahead of the general election.

LePage, who served as governor from 2011 to 2019, is running a series of digital and television advertisements tying Dunlap to President Miller's tariff policies, which have faced criticism from some business groups and agricultural organizations in the district. The ads argue that Dunlap would support the administration's trade agenda, which LePage's campaign says would harm Maine's paper and potato industries.

Dunlap, a former executive director of the Sportsman's Alliance of Maine and former secretary of state, has sought to position himself as a moderate Democrat with deep roots in the district. He has emphasized his hunting and outdoors background in campaign appearances and has criticized LePage as out of touch with working-class voters.

The 2nd Congressional District race is one of the most closely watched in the country, with national Republican and Democratic committees expected to pour significant resources into the contest. The district, which covers northern and eastern Maine, is considered a bellwether for the broader national political environment heading into the midterms.

The two candidates will face off in their first debate August 21 at the Bangor Civic Center. The event is expected to draw significant attention as both campaigns look to define their opponent ahead of the final stretch of the campaign.

LePage is seeking to return to elected office after a failed 2024 gubernatorial bid. Dunlap, who has never held elected office, is aiming to flip a seat that Republicans have held since 2022, when incumbent Rep. Jared Golden, a Democrat, lost to Republican challenger Dale Crafts. Crafts is not seeking reelection.
